statement: You are given a binary tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.

Give the root column 0; a left child sits one column to the left of its parent (column − 1) and a right child one column to the right (column + 1). Looking up at the tree from below, you see in each column only its lowest node. If two nodes in a column are equally low, the one that comes later in a level-order traversal is the one seen.
Return the values seen from below, ordered from the leftmost column to the rightmost.

examples.explanation: 3, the right child of 8, sits in column 0 below the root 20, so it is seen instead of 20. Every other column holds a single node.
Each of the three nodes has a column to itself.
5 and 6 are both in column 0 on the bottom level. 6 comes later in level order, so it is the one seen.
